title: A ShieldCare Plan Held While a Claim Is Under Review
content:
## Why a plan is held

A claim on a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan that needs an inspection, a police report or a
second opinion puts the plan into a hold, so that only one claim is worked at a time.

## How long a review may run

A claim is held under review for no longer than the plan's review days, counted from the day the
claim was opened. Review days are counted as business days on the retailer's trading calendar
from the day the claim was opened, which counts as day zero, and days the stores are shut do not
count. The recorded day the claim was opened is the anchor, the count is correlated to the claim
reference, and the release may fall no later than the end of those review days; a release on the
last of them is inside the rule.

### Both sides of the review count

On a plan carrying 7 review days, with the claim opened on day zero, a release on the seventh
trading day afterwards is inside the rule, and a release on the eighth trading day is not. Two
days on which the stores are shut inside that run do not count toward the seven, so the seventh
trading day falls two calendar days later than it otherwise would.

## How a hold ends

The hold is released when the decision is recorded, when the customer withdraws, or when the
review days run out, in which case the claim is decided on the evidence then on file.

## What a hold does not do

Cover is not suspended by a hold: the coverage window keeps running and the term still ends on
its own day.

A plan on a tier with priority claim handling is reviewed ahead of the ordinary queue, which
shortens the wait but does not change the review days themselves.
